technical-data.invention-title: ELECTRIC ENERGY OUTPUT MECHANISM THROUGH CYLINDERS MOMENTUM AND ANGULAR MOMENTUM
MECANISME DE PRODUCTION ELECTRIQUE UTILISANT L'ELAN ET L'ELAN ANGULAIRE DE CYLINDRES

abstract.p: The invention concerns an arrangement of cylinders (1) being rolled at high speed on concentric circular tracks (3). The outermost rail (4) of each track is higher than the innermost one to damp out the effect of the centrifugal force. The center of the initial outermost periphery has a diameter of 2.000 meters. The tracks carry a multitude of cylinders separated by 160 cm along the outermost track. In this space there is placed an engine pulling a group of coupled cylinders. Under the rails shafts are placed which are radially extended from the outermost track towards the center of the circle. The shafts bear pistons (5) protruding between the rails of said tracks. Upon the impact of the cylinders on the pistons the energy of the cylinders is transmitted to the shafts which are being driven at the same speed.

L'invention concerne un agencement de cylindres (1) roulant à grande vitesse sur des pistes circulaires concentriques (3). Le rail le plus externe (4) de chaque piste est plus élevé que le rail le plus interne afin d'amortir la force centrifuge. Le centre de la périphérie initiale la plus externe a un diamètre de 2,000 mètres. Les pistes portent plusieurs cylindres séparés par 160 cm le long de la piste la plus externe. Dans cet espace, on a placé un engin tirant un groupe de cylindres couplés. Sous les rails, on a placé des arbres s'étendant radialement de la piste la plus externe en direction du centre du cercle. Les arbres portent des pistons (5) saillant entre les rails desdites pistes. Lors de l'impact des cylindres contre les pistons, l'énergie des cylindres est transmise aux arbres qui sont entraînés à la même vitesse.

This invention is based on the law of inertia. A cylinder pulled, by a machine in a horizontal surface following the desired speed, is moved to its motor energy, due to inertia.
However, it gets energy (consumes) from the machine it is 5 pulling the cylinder to eliminate the untoward frictions as well as the air resistance so as to maintain its motor status.
If we just deem a cylinder moving in a horizontal surface without any friction at all as well as any air resistance, ±0 it shall move forever in any speed, whatsoever.
The cylinder on moving, bears an energy being proportionate to its speed.
The more its speed is increasing, the more its energy increases. 15 The energy the cylinder bears is an acquisition of its inertia.

The transfer (transmission) of a body from a point to another point by means of the force of a certain energy, is called work. The energy required for the production of a 3-0 work is always the same irrespective of time.
E.G. If a is the energy for the production of a work at a speed of 5 kilometers per hour. Again a shall be if we just double the velocity or we just triple it.

Because at the time of doubling a double action shall be 35 required, but at the 1/2 of time that is A x 2 : 2 = a and while in the tripling procedure is a x 3 : 3 = a. It is the law of energy preservation.
The action is not the same for the work yielded in several velocities through the cylinder's momentum (impetus) and angular momentum.

Each increased speed of the cylinder also bears an every ό increased actin and the work produced is obtained at a decreased energy against the previous velocity and this is quite contrary to the law of nature in respect to the action maintenance.
By means of the experiments that I am going to perform, all 10 of the above mentioned shall be fully confirmed.

The mechanism consists of six (6) concetric peripheries and each of them consists of rails couple supported on a horizontal ground or flat surface on an iron construction of beams of a double T of a cross-section. The outermost rail of each periphery is higher than the innermost periphery according to the gradient required to avoid any centrifugal forces .
On each rails couple, cylinders are moving giving a revolution by means of an impact (pressure) to shaft i pistons.
